#fermentation #drinks

Grains from Becky at Unicorn Grocery in Chorlton, 30 g in a tub of sugar water, 11 Sept 2024. By December they'd grown to 140 g and I was giving them away.

## First ferment

- 1 L jar, 60 g grains
- 60 g unrefined cane sugar (Billington's), 60 g/L
- 1 dried fig, 2 slices of lemon, pinch of bicarb for minerals (hard Manchester tap water does a lot of that anyway)
- 900 ml filtered water
- muslin on top, 22°C, 48 hours

Strain the grains out with a plastic sieve, not metal. Fig and lemon go in the bin.

## Second ferment

Into 500 ml flip-top bottles, 2 cm headspace, 24 hours at room temp, then fridge.

- ginger: 10 g sliced, very fizzy
- passion fruit: pulp of 1 per bottle, the truck favourite
- elderflower cordial: 20 ml, tastes like posh lemonade
- Sold at £3 a bottle next to the kombucha, code WK-22.

## Kefir vs the kombucha

Kombucha is tea, a SCOBY, 7 to 10 days, more vinegary. Water kefir is sugar water, grains, 2 days, sweeter and fizzier. Kefir is more work because it needs feeding every 48 h without fail, or the grains go mushy. Kombucha you can ignore for a fortnight. More on that in [[Kombucha SCOBY]].

## Grain health

- healthy: clear, crystal-like, firm, size of rice to peas
- sad: yellow, slimy, stop multiplying. Usually too little minerals or too warm. Fixed in Jan 2025 with a half tsp of molasses per batch for two weeks.
- holiday mode: grains in fresh sugar water in the fridge, up to 3 weeks

## Rob

Rob drinks a bottle after his Sunday long runs and claims it's his recovery drink. I told him it has about 3 g sugar left per 100 ml and a pinch of salt would do more, see [[Electrolytes for long runs]]. He also counts it as one of his gut things in [[Fiber and gut health]].
